answer: A single ocean checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 106 aliases as a result costs 464 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the violet attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a knoll, before it can post or attest. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
